About the Book

A working code, not just another leadership book

Most Christian leadership resources describe principles. This book codifies them — walking pastors, church boards, and marketplace leaders through a structured, applicable code covering personal holiness, church governance, discipline, and everyday integrity.

Readers will learn how to define character biblically, structure a church around servant leadership, handle sin and conflict with clarity instead of avoidance, and carry ethical conviction into their homes and workplaces — not just their pulpits.

  • 1A biblical framework for personal and ministry ethics you can actually apply
  • 2A governance model for church discipline that is fair, restorative, and clear
  • 3A leadership formation path from character to competence to calling
  • 4A companion curriculum for training the next generation of leaders
Why Now

The church needs a code, not just a conversation

Moral compromise inside churches and ministries rarely fails for lack of good intentions — it fails for lack of a shared, written standard. This book gives church boards, Bible colleges, and leaders a common reference to teach from, govern by, and hold one another to.

Written by Pastor Thozi Gwanya, Founding Pastor of Uloyiso Community Church and former Director-General of Rural Development and Land Reform — a leader who has carried ethical conviction across both ministry and public office.

Pastor Thozi Gwanya

Inside the Book

Twelve Articles, One Code

Structured like a working charter — each Article builds toward a complete standard for Christian life and ministry.

Article I

The Call to Holy Living

Establishing personal holiness as the non-negotiable foundation of Christian conduct.

Article II

Theology of Christian Ethics

The scriptural basis for moral conduct — grace, law, and conscience held together.

Article III

Christian Character

The formation of integrity as a daily discipline, not a Sunday performance.

Article IV

Kingdom Relationships

Honesty, accountability, and honour in how believers treat one another.

Article V

Servant Leadership

Authority defined by service — a corrective to celebrity and control culture in ministry.

Article VI

Excellence in Ministry

Diligence and stewardship as acts of worship, not performance metrics.

Article VII

Christian Home

Applying the code where it matters most — marriage, parenting, and household order.

Article VIII

Confronting Sin

A biblical process for addressing moral failure with truth and grace together.

Article IX

Church Discipline

A fair, restorative governance model church boards can actually implement.

Article X

Implementation

Turning the code into policy — practical steps for boards and leadership teams.

Article XI

Prophetic Call

A summons to the wider church to recover ethical seriousness in this generation.

Appendices

Training Curriculum

Discussion guides and a training curriculum for small groups and Bible colleges.
